name: upkeep
description: Cross-platform system cleanup and updater. v1.6 ports the single-shot update orchestrator (scripts/update.sh) to Linux and WSL2 — one OS-aware fast path for macOS, Linux, and WSL2, replacing the old per-platform flows. On Linux, language tools, snap, and flatpak are auto-applied; apt/dnf/pacman upgrades are surfaced as manual sudo steps (never run — upkeep never uses sudo). On WSL2, Windows package managers (winget/scoop/choco) are audit-only. The skill is a thin two-turn wrapper: turn 1 builds the plan and renders one approval gate, turn 2 applies and reports. brew-update TTL caching (1h default) keeps macOS warm runs <5s. The deterministic pattern-table failure diagnoser (scripts/diagnose.sh) now covers Linux failures too (dpkg/apt lock, dnf metadata/conflict, snap change-in-progress, flatpak runtime-missing) alongside the macOS patterns. All v1.2-v1.5 security invariants preserved: hardcoded dispatcher allowlist (apt/dnf/pacman excluded by design), discovery JSON sanitization, exact-match remote URL validation, trust-on-first-use, plan/apply turn separation, canonical-path containment, TOCTOU-safe plan write. Five entry points: deep, quick, audit, update, upkeep.
